newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia April new vehicle sales up yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia April new vehicle sales up yr/yr.

text.p: Australian new vehicle sales for April 1997 fell 2.1 percent from their March level but were 16.5 percent higher than April last year, the Federal Chamber of Automotive Industries (FCAI) said on Wednesday.

Sales totalled 56,284 against 57,472 in March and 48,295 in April 1996. For the year to date, sales were running ahead of 1996 by 6.5 percent and the FCAI said it was revising up its forecast for sales in the entire year by 10,000 to 640,000.
In April, the passenger vehicle market grew by 14.3 percent over the same month last year, but was down 2.1 percent on March, while truck sales were 23.6 percent higher year-on-year.
Year-to-date, the total passenger vehicle market was up by 8,230 vehicles or 5.3 percent due to continued strength in the small car segment, which rose by 24.7 percent.
Solid performances came from the sports car sector which rose 1,068 or 38.14 percent, and the luxury car segment which was up by 1,181 or 28.5 percent in comparison to the four months to April 1996.
The medium car sector firmed in April but was still down by 3,578 units or 20.2 percent for the year to date.
The light truck market recorded an increase of 4,727 vehicles or 10.9 percent ahead of 1996, with a particularly strong performance by the all terrain wagon segment, FCAI said.
The heavy truck market was running 5.2 percent ahead of the same period in 1996.

Ford Motor Co was the market leader in April and also holds the top spot for the year-to-date with a market share of 18.7 percent. This was down on the 19.9 percent held in the first four months of 1996.
In second place was General Motors Corp with a 17.2 percent market share, followed by Toyota Motor Corp with 16.3 percent.
